extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of mass communication, journalism researchers, and advanced journalism practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying analytical dimensions and evaluative criteria used in media studies to assess news content, newsroom behavior, and institutional influences on journalism. Useful for coding content, designing newsroom assessments, or teaching media-effects and political communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy in Media (index entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a topical concern (index references). Treated as an evaluative dimension of news quality and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias (definition and political bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias — changes in newspapers' ; defined; political (index references: 'Bias changes in newspapers', 'defined', 'political, 42-44, 166-167').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess bias both conceptually (how defined) and empirically (changes and political slant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisers' influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisers, influence of (index entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific effects such as influence on children's television programming and audience targeting; used to evaluate commercial pressures on content selection and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience targeting by advertisers
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisers: targeting of audiences (index references 191-194).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how content or placement is shaped to reach demographic groups advertisers want to target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience routines and consumer/audience routines
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience routines; Consumer/audience routines, 110-117 (index entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider routines of audiences (when/how they consume) as a factor shaping news production and story placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience effects (media effects on pictures of the world)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience and effects; News influence on our pictures of the world (McCombs & Gilbert).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use agenda-setting, cultivation, and dependency perspectives to evaluate how news shapes audience perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gatekeeping / Gatekeepers
rubrics_metrics.description: Gatekeepers; keeping the gates for gatekeepers (index entries: 105-106, 117-118, 119).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate selection and omission decisions, including role of wire services and editorial filters, in determining what becomes news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines (effects on news content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines, effects of (index entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how temporal production pressures influence accuracy, depth, sourcing, and story selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity as a news-selection factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Proximity of event as factor in selection of news sources (index reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure how geographic or social closeness of events influences whether and how they are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviance as predictor of newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviance, depicted by the media; Deviance as a predictor of newsworthiness (multiple references, e.g., Shoemaker et al.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the extent to which deviant acts, scandals, or riskiness increase selection and prominence of stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source prominence and dominance
rubrics_metrics.description: The prominence and dominance of news sources in newspaper medical coverage (index entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whose voices appear most and how dominance of certain sources shapes framing and balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-press relationship / source-selection characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Source-press relationship: major characteristics of sources which influence selection of sources in news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider accessibility, authority, resources, and relationships between journalists and sources when evaluating sourcing patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations' influence on the news
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations' influence on the news; Public relations versus journalism (Shoemaker references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate use of PR materials/information subsidies and their effect on story content, frequency, and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermedia influence / flow between media
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermedia influence and the flow of news between media (e.g., 'Intermedia influence and the drug issue', 'Flow of news between Canada and the United States').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how stories propagate across outlets and how dominant outlets shape agendas and frames in others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and economic effects on content
rubrics_metrics.description: Economics, effects of on content; Effect of monopoly in Cleveland on diversity of newspaper content; Press concentration and monopoly (index entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how ownership structures, consolidation, and profit motives affect diversity, story choice, and editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market competition's impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition, marketplace (index entry); impact of intercity competition on daily newspaper content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure changes in content, format, and presentation driven by competition among news outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls and censorship (legal/regulatory environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls/censorship: First Amendment freedoms; government policies and actions; international regulations/laws; regulations/laws in the United States (index entries 202-209, 199-202, 203-205).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how legal frameworks, government pressure, and international constraints shape what can be reported and how.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Information / FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of Information rules; FOIA policy directives issued (index references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate access to public information and how FOI regimes facilitate or hinder reporting and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness Doctrine and related broadcast rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness Doctrine (1949) (index entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how obligations (or their removal) to present balanced coverage influence broadcast news content and editorial choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and professional codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics; Society of Professional Journalists Code of Ethics (index entries 95-102).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate journalistic conduct against established ethical standards: accuracy, fairness, harm minimization, independence, transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity and the news paradigm / ideology of objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The news paradigm and the ideology of objectivity; ideology (index references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this dimension to assess whether and how objectivity norms shape story structure, sourcing, and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of graphic devices and design
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of graphic devices in a competitive situation (case study reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate visual presentation, graphics, and layout choices as contributors to salience, comprehension, and persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire services and their effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping the gates for gatekeepers: The effects of wire news (index references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess homogenization, reliance on wire copy, and its effect on local distinctiveness and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public broadcasting editorializing
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Unshackled but unwilling: Public broadcasting and editorializing' (index reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate editorial stances and restrictions on advocacy within public broadcasters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnic, gender, and demographic depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic groups depicted on (index); gender; elderly; demographic patterns (index references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess representation, stereotyping, and inclusiveness across different social groups in news content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groupthink / pack mentality among journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Groupthink/pack mentality of communicators/journalists (index entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate evidence of routinized consensus, homogenized framing, or herding behavior in coverage choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda-setting (media influence on public salience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda-setting function of mass media (McCombs & Shaw reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to measure how media prominence of issues correlates with public perceptions of issue importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivation and long-term media effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Living with television: The dynamics of the cultivation process (Gerbner references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess long-term exposure effects on audience perceptions of reality (e.g., violence profiles, fear of crime).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content categories and measurement (entertainment vs news; correlation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Media content category: Correlation, entertainment vs news, content analysis methods (index references to content categories and correlation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify and quantify content types (news, entertainment) and use correlation methods to evaluate relationships among variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story selection criteria — prominence, drama, events
rubrics_metrics.description: Events and dramatic stories; pseudo-events; news as purposive behavior (references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate story selection using classic newsworthiness criteria: prominence, timeliness, drama, conflict, and pseudo-events.
